Docs.summary: Extends with metadata-carrying counterparts of its three header-creation methods. Each returns the full (header value, binding certificate, and token-acquisition metadata) as an instead of a bare header string.
Docs.remarks: Follows the additive numeric-suffix interface-evolution convention: the new interface extends the existing one so a single implementation can serve both, and existing string-returning callers are unaffected. The user, application, and unified entry points mirror the inputs of , , and respectively; when the selected protocol is bound (for example mTLS Proof-of-Possession) the binding certificate is populated on the returned .

The containing information about the API to be called and token acquisition settings. If not provided, the header will be for a bearer token.

Inbound authentication elements. In a web API, this is usually the result of the validation of a token. In a web app, this would be information about the signed-in user.
